newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA STRESSES REGIONAL VIEW IN EU TRADE TALKS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA STRESSES REGIONAL VIEW IN EU TRADE TALKS.

text.p: South Africa could not reach a bilateral trade agreement with the European Union that impacted negatively on its neighbours, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Thursday.

Opening the Southern African Development Community (SADC) parliamentary forum's plenary assembly meeting, Mbeki said that South Africa had been widely criticised for the slowness with which the negotiations were taking place.
"The European Union is losing patience with us for moving too slowly," Mbeki said.
The main reason for this was South Africa's concern that its agreement with the EU should not have a negative impact on other SADC states.
"That is an illustration of how much the fact of SADC impacts on domestic policies," he said.
In particular, South Africa believed that SADC products should take priority over products from the EU.

At a recent parliamentary workshop for SADC states, South Africa was criticised by some delegates for not ratifying a SADC trade protocol before finalising its negotiations with the EU. Officials said the negotiations were linked.
Mbeki said that SADC states were co-operating on a wide range of issues which would play an important role in the development of the region.
These ranges from the development of transport and communications infrastructure to tourism and security.

Mbeki said the missing link in all these developments was the closer involvement of ordinary SADC citizens in the process and he said he would like to see the SADC secretariat making regular report backs to individual parliaments in SADC countries.
SADC members states are Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Swaziland, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzanaia, Mauritius, Namibia, Mozambique and Malawi.
The assembly will on Friday consider reports from several recent meetings held in the run-up to the establishment of the parliamentary forum.
